accuracy.evidence: Checked: DfE 'Mobile phones in schools' (February 2024) is non-statutory guidance that allows exceptions such as medical needs; Beland and Murphy (LSE, 2015) found test score gains after bans in four English cities, largest for low attainers; Goodyear et al. (Lancet Regional Health Europe, 2025) compared 30 secondary schools and found no wellbeing difference.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips in ethical reasoning: treating a values question as a fact question, popularity as a reason, strawmanning the other side, ignoring evidence that goes against you, and one-size rules that miss a medical exception.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstance works one live issue end to end: a fact/values card sort, a stakeholder match, a draggable position marker that must agree with its reason, a steelman-or-strawman pick and an evidence sort; flagdilem's value clash and consequence balance are not reused.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each wrong drop or pick explains itself, e.g. 'Fair is a values word', 'That reason supports the other side. Move Me', 'That is a strawman', so the learner finds the rule by acting before the done message names it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions carry tempting wrong options the lab tests: that a ban can be looked up, that a rule hits everyone the same, that popular reasons are strongest, and that you should ignore evidence against your view.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six Challenge questions with twelve specific slip messages, e.g. 'Lots of people agreeing is popularity, not a reason.' and 'The same rule can hurt someone with a medical need.'

mobile.evidence: On an iPhone 13 the cards wrap inside large tap areas, every drag has a button twin (bins, Against/For, Reason 1-3, Summary A-C), and the lab passed the phone walkthrough.

no_filler.evidence: Every step opens with the action and its reason; no warm-up phrases. The adult text goes straight to the curriculum link, the real guidance and evidence, and the common mistakes.

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences for 9 to 11 year olds and explains fact, values, reason and evidence in plain words; numbers in items stay within simple addition and subtraction.

accessibility.evidence: Canvas aria-label updates after every action, all controls are labelled buttons with aria-pressed on the reasons, card text is dark ink on light fills in both themes, and reduced motion speeds up Show me.
